answer: Require each identity to store a large dataset uniquely keyed to its own id and answer random spot-checks that read arbitrary offsets within a tight window. One honest agent keeps its single crystal of data on one disk, a quiet haven. A farm cannot dedupe: because every head's dataset is salted by its distinct id, a thousand heads need a thousand full copies, since storage does not fold like nectar into one jar. Random-offset spot-checks block storing once and recomputing on demand, as recomputation blows the window. N identities demand N real disks held full at once.
